title: Stop Distance vs Dollar Risk
hook: Points describe the chart. Dollars describe the account.

launchpad.outcome: Separate how far the stop is from what the stop costs.

slides.heading: Two traders, one sentence
slides.punch: “They both said they use a 30-point stop.” True.

slides.title: Which question does each one answer?
“My stop is only 20 points, so this is low risk.”

options.label: Yes, 20 points is small
options.feedback: Small in points. Unknown in dollars.

options.label: No: missing the instrument and the contracts

slides.punch: POINTS DESCRIBE THE CHART. DOLLARS DESCRIBE THE ACCOUNT.

slides.quote: Points describe the chart. Dollars describe the account.

slides.prompt: Why doesn’t “I use a 30-point stop” describe your risk?
slides.modelAnswer: Because the dollar risk also depends on the instrument’s value per point and the number of contracts. Two traders with the same stop can risk completely different amounts.

takeaways: Ask: how far, what’s it worth, how many.
remember: Points describe the chart. Dollars describe the account.
